proof_summary: Explicit finite witness tables handle the bounded Goldbach and Lemoine cases, while above the thresholds positivity supplies a prime \(q\) such that \(n-q\) (for even \(n\)) or \(n-2q\) (for odd \(n\)) is prime, yielding the required decompositions. For any bound \(N\), applying the even case to \(n=2N+8028\) gives \(2q<n\), so \((n-q-6,n-q)\) is a cousin-prime pair whose first member exceeds \(N\), proving infinitude.
